current.text: He is back playing after a broken foot that needed surgery.
Experts expect him to be ready for opening night.
Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa. Davis plays center on offense, and Sarr plays more power forward and switches on the perimeter. He is a projected starter.
Experts expect his usage to fall. Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa push him to the fourth or fifth offensive option, so they do not expect a third-year breakout.
His minutes should go up, but he should touch the ball less per minute.
Experts expect fewer rim contests, blocks and rebounds next to Anthony Davis, and more threes with a lower FG%. One projection is 13 points, 7 rebounds and 1.9 blocks.
Experts call his Yahoo rank of 56 too high. They would not draft him in the 50s or 60s. One gives a best case of 62nd and a worst case of 134th.
Experts call him a fair pick from about 80 to 90. In mock drafts he went between 81 and 87. One expert took him at 87 only because he needed a center and would normally let him fall further.
His upside depends on Anthony Davis. Rank 56 only makes sense if Davis plays fewer than 40 games. If Davis is traded, Sarr starts at center. One expert is about 80% sure Washington keeps Davis.
Washington is trying to compete and is projected to win about 40 games. The late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not return.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under pressure to win games this season.

durable.text: He is a heavy rim protector. He led the league in contested shots at the rim by a wide margin and was second in blocks at 2.0 per game.
Blocks are his clear standout category, far above the top 250 pool. The two sites disagree on how many he keeps: Yahoo projects 1.2 per game and ESPN 2.0.
His FG% depends on where he shoots. It is much higher when he plays near the rim than when he takes many threes.
He has a history of a broken foot that needed surgery.

note: Experts agree Sarr is a blocks source priced too high at Yahoo rank 56 (value 18 USD). They put him at picks 80 to 90, which fits his ESPN value of 7 USD and the 9 USD he cost in our league last season more than Yahoo's number. In our auction he is worth paying up to about 10 USD for a blocks build, since his 2.0 BLK with FT% near 70% suits a team that already gives up some FT%. Early in the season, check whether he plays power forward next to Anthony Davis, and whether his blocks stay near ESPN's 2.0 or fall toward Yahoo's 1.2. Also watch his FG% as his threes rise, and any Davis injury or trade, which would put Sarr back at center.
